solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Imposing, most of place where the US Masters golf is played

indicators.note: most of says the word loses its final letter, keeping all but the tail

parts.words: place where the US Masters golf is played
parts.note: the Masters golf tournament is held at Augusta National in Augusta, Georgia

explanation.surface: A golf commentator admires the grand setting of the Masters course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last A from AUGUSTA, the Georgia city that hosts the Masters.
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective means majestic and inspiring awe, a close synonym of imposing.

clue.text: Delegate when cross

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a cross is a sign, such as the X marking a signature

explanation.surface: A manager hands work over whenever angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like an adjective meaning angry, but it is the noun: a cross is a sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To delegate a task is to hand it to someone else, which is the verb sense of assign.

clue.text: A diver, seabird after catching one, soaring to me

indicators.note: catching means the bird's name takes the numeral inside it

parts.note: a gull is a common seabird
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: soaring, in a down clue, says the words to me are read upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: A diving bird swoops towards the speaker after snatching something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A diver' looks like a person, but it is the bird; 'soaring' reverses in a down clue because the letters read upwards. 'after' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The guillemot is a seabird that dives underwater from the surface to hunt fish.

clue.text: Separate FBI agents in series

indicators.note: in places the agents inside the word for series

parts.note: a set is a series or collection of things
G-men is slang for FBI agents, government men

explanation.surface: Federal agents are split up into a sequence of groups.
explanation.definitionFit: To segment something is to divide it into parts, a verb synonym of separate.

clue.text: One holding a sword, blackleg confronting poet

indicators.note: confronting puts the first piece facing the second, ahead of it in the answer

parts.note: a blackleg is a strikebreaker, also called a scab
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A swordsman, a strikebreaker, squares up to a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: A blackleg is British for someone who works during a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is the sheath that holds a sword when it is not in use.

clue.text: Wren, perhaps, and others chirp away

indicators.note: away suggests the letters fly off and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A wren and other birds go off chirping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wren' looks like the bird, which the chirping supports; it is the architect Sir Christopher Wren, and 'perhaps' marks him as one example of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Christopher Wren, architect of St Paul's Cathedral, is one bearer of this first name.

clue.text: Showing off, supporter meeting five before a party

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
V is the Roman numeral for five
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A fan shows off by going to a party with five friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a boastful show of boldness, which is a form of showing off.

clue.text: Space around new stadium

indicators.note: around says the space word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: an area is a space

explanation.surface: There is room around a newly built sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed venue for sport or shows, a stadium.

clue.text: Set off from college in time

indicators.note: in places the college inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a time when something happens
Eton College is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: Someone sets out from college right on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set off' reads as depart, but it means explode.
explanation.definitionFit: To detonate a bomb is to set it off, making it explode.

clue.text: Mean and waspish?

definitions.meaning: mean as in miserly, unwilling to spend
playfully, like a wasp, which has a sting; the question mark flags the pun

explanation.definitionFit: Stingy means miserly, and read literally it describes something with a sting, like a wasp.

clue.text: Celebrity wearing badly torn accessory

indicators.note: wearing means the rearranged letters are worn round the celebrity word
badly says the letters of torn are put in poor order

parts.note: a name is a celebrity, as in 'a big name'

explanation.surface: A star wears a ripped accessory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Celebrity' as a noun meaning a big name is easy to miss; 'badly' scrambles the fodder and 'wearing' wraps it around the name.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament is a decorative object or trinket, which can serve as an accessory.

clue.text: More than one museum in large isle abroad

indicators.note: abroad suggests the letters are scattered widely into a new order

explanation.surface: There are several museums on a big island overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Galleries are buildings that display art, a kind of museum, and the plural matches more than one.

clue.text: Irish train soon loaded with emergency supplies of food

indicators.note: loaded, meaning drunk, signals the letters are reeling into another order

explanation.surface: An Irish train will soon be loaded with food for a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded' reads as filled with cargo, but it means drunk, shuffling IR, TRAIN and SOON.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron rations are a small emergency food supply carried by soldiers or travellers.

clue.text: Commander elected once more

parts.note: an aga is a commander in the Ottoman Empire
in means elected, as a party voted in

explanation.surface: The commander has been voted in for another term.
explanation.definitionFit: Again means once more, a second time.

clue.text: Weatherman ran across English mapper of mountains

parts.note: met means ran across, encountered
an orologist studies and describes mountains

explanation.surface: A TV forecaster bumped into an English mountain surveyor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran across' looks like movement but means MET; orology is the study of mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteorologist forecasts weather, a weatherman in everyday speech.

clue.text: At home, soldier with no one else present

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
a private is a soldier of the lowest rank

explanation.surface: A soldier stays at home alone.
explanation.definitionFit: In private means away from others, with nobody else there to see or hear.

clue.text: Blow up theatre put up by canal

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: put up, in a down clue, says the theatre word is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
a cut is a canal, an artificial waterway

explanation.surface: Someone wants to blow up a theatre built beside a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow up' looks like a phrase; 'Blow' alone is the definition and 'up' supplies UP. 'put up' turns REP into PER.
explanation.definitionFit: An uppercut is a punch thrown upwards to the chin, a kind of blow.

clue.text: The loquacious poker player may be told to raise or fold

definitions.text: The loquacious poker player may be told to raise or fold

parts.words: The loquacious poker player may be told to raise or fold
parts.note: a talkative card player is told either to stake more money or to stop talking, both demands in one idiom

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom challenges someone to act on their claims or stay quiet, here applied to betting and chatter.

clue.text: Soldier, in consequence, left umbrella

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier
so means in consequence, therefore

explanation.surface: A soldier therefore left an umbrella behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a light umbrella used for shade from the sun.

clue.text: Advertisement for a mobile home

definitions.meaning: a preview of a film shown to advertise it
in American usage, a home towed or parked on a site

explanation.definitionFit: A trailer is both a film preview and, in North America, a caravan or mobile home.

clue.text: Portable shelter sheltering an occupant

indicators.note: sheltering says the tent word covers the next piece inside it

parts.note: a tent is a portable shelter

explanation.surface: A tent shelters someone living in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant is one who occupies rented property, an occupant.

clue.text: Mistake admitted by conjuror, really taken aback

indicators.note: taken aback says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A magician owns up to a blunder, genuinely startled.
explanation.walkthrough: The run RORRE sits across 'conjuror, really'; 'by' marks it hidden and 'taken aback' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, and one that has been admitted is still an error.

clue.text: Kingdom in actual miles

parts.note: real means actual

explanation.surface: A kingdom measured in genuine miles.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom, the territory ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Avert shock by A-team?

parts.note: a turn is a shock, as in 'it gave me a turn'
an A side is a first team

explanation.surface: A top team might prevent a sudden fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gave me a turn' is a British idiom for a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn aside something is to avert it, deflecting it away.

clue.text: TV programme, extremely childish — so what's new?

indicators.note: extremely picks the extremes, the outer letters, of childish
new signals the letters of so what are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the 's is the clue's 'is', not a letter

explanation.surface: A viewer dismisses a puerile television show as nothing novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes CH from childish; 'new' rearranges SO WHAT to ATSHOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat show is a television programme of conversation with guests.

clue.text: Animal coming from mountain, a cat with no tail

parts.note: an alp is a mountain

indicators.note: with no tail means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A tailless cat comes down from the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpaca is a South American animal related to the llama.

clue.text: Parisian's article in newspaper is classic

indicators.note: in places the article inside the newspaper

parts.note: The Times is a newspaper
les is a French plural definite article

explanation.surface: A French article in a newspaper is a classic.
explanation.definitionFit: Timeless means never going out of date, as a classic is.

clue.text: Bother about religious instruction? I surely do

definitions.text: Bother about religious instruction? I surely do

indicators.note: about says the nuisance word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: a pest is a bother, a nuisance

explanation.surface: A cleric declares that worrying over religious teaching is his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' marks the container; the whole clue is a cleric speaking about himself, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman cares about religious teaching, so the whole clue describes the speaker.
